audit.scope: 38 Domain E seed QIDs (Pack C: 19, Pack D: 19)

seed_items.Stem: Driftwood assigns one employee to authorize purchases, another to record them, and a third to reconcile the vendor accounts. What internal control concept does this reflect?
Hearthstone evaluates its internal control system using a widely recognized framework consisting of five integrated components. What framework is this?
Nightingale's internal auditors assess opportunity, pressure, and rationalization when evaluating fraud risk in a department. What model are they applying?
Thornfield stores inventory in a locked warehouse accessible only to authorized personnel with badge access. What type of control is this?

seed_items.Topic: E.021 segregation of duties vendor setup and payment
seed_items.Stem: Bryant Manufacturing has a small accounts payable department where one employee creates new vendor records, enters invoices from those vendors, and approves payments for processing. Management wants to reduce the risk of fraudulent payments without adding staff. Which control improvement is most effective?

seed_items.Topic: E.022 preventive vs detective duplicate payment control
seed_items.Stem: Crestview Manufacturing frequently discovers duplicate vendor payments when reviewing the monthly accounts payable aging report. Management wants to implement a control that will best prevent duplicates from occurring. Which one of the following controls is preventive?

seed_items.Topic: E.023 IT access control terminated employee deprovisioning
seed_items.Stem: During an internal audit, Drake Distribution discovered that a former employee's system access remained active for 18 days after termination. No unauthorized transactions occurred during that period. Management wants to prevent recurrence. Which remediation is most appropriate?

seed_items.Topic: E.024 application input control sales order validation
seed_items.Stem: Parkview Company's sales order system accepts orders with invalid customer codes, negative quantities, and missing ship-to addresses. These errors are discovered only when invoices fail to process days later. Which application control would best address this issue?
Zenith Bay requires dual signatures on checks above a threshold before payment is released. Is this a preventive or detective control, and why?
Copperline has a designated employee, independent of cash handling and recording, perform the monthly bank reconciliation. Why is independence important here?
Foxglove's board defines the amount of risk the organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives. What enterprise risk management concept is being defined?
Oleander requires periodic review of user access rights to ensure employees only retain system access appropriate to their current role. What category of control is this?
Pinehollow's CEO instructs the controller to bypass a normal approval control to record a favorable adjusting entry near year-end. What internal control limitation does this illustrate?
Yorkshire establishes an anonymous reporting channel for employees to report suspected fraud or ethical violations without fear of retaliation. What internal control objective does this serve?
Cliffside is too small to fully segregate duties among its few accounting employees. What can help mitigate this control weakness?

seed_items.Topic: E.060 control environment tone at top
seed_items.Stem: Knollwood's board and senior executives consistently emphasize integrity and ethical behavior, which shapes employee attitudes toward compliance. What COSO component does this describe?

seed_items.Topic: E.061 inherent risk vs control risk
seed_items.Stem: Lanternwood's auditor assesses the susceptibility of an account to material misstatement before considering any related controls. What type of risk is being assessed?
Quailrun has the same employee both handling incoming cash receipts and recording them in the accounting records. What control weakness does this create?

Willowmere identifies a control deficiency during its internal control assessment and assigns an owner, a corrective action plan, and a target completion date. What internal control process is being followed?

seed_items.Topic: E.001 three lines of defense model
seed_items.Stem: Alderway structures its risk and control functions using operational management, risk/compliance oversight, and internal audit as distinct layers. What model is this?
Juniperfield grants employees system access limited only to what is necessary to perform their specific job duties. What security principle is being applied?
Northfell has a supervisor recount inventory counted by warehouse staff before finalizing the count. What type of control activity is this?
Palisade decides to purchase insurance to address a significant identified risk rather than eliminate the underlying activity. What enterprise risk management response is this?
Zionsgate requires that all purchase orders above a certain dollar amount be approved by a manager before the order is placed. What type of control activity is this?

Crownridge's management periodically reviews exception reports and reconciliations as part of regular operations to assess whether controls are functioning as intended. What COSO component does this represent?
Jettison maintains offsite backups of critical financial data and a documented plan for restoring systems after a disruption. What control objective does this address?

seed_items.Topic: E.036 change management control it systems
seed_items.Stem: Kirkwood requires all software changes to be tested, approved, and documented before being moved into the production environment. What type of control is this?
Quarrycrest's risk management team scores identified risks based on their likelihood of occurring and the potential impact if they do. What process is this?

seed_items.Topic: E.046 code of conduct ethics program
seed_items.Stem: Umberglen requires all employees to complete annual ethics training and sign an acknowledgment of the company's code of conduct. What internal control component does this primarily support?
seed_items.Subtopic: Code of conduct and ethics program

seed_items.Stem: Briarcliff requires multi-factor authentication for all employees accessing financial systems remotely. What is the primary purpose of this control?

seed_items.Topic: E.058 internal control cost benefit limitation
seed_items.Stem: Ivorycrest's management decides not to implement an extremely costly control because the risk it addresses is low and infrequent. What limitation of internal control does this illustrate?
Oakvale restricts the ability to add or modify vendor records to a small group of employees separate from those who approve invoice payments. What risk does this control primarily address?
Quillwood's board audit committee oversees the financial reporting process, the external auditor relationship, and the internal audit function. What is the primary purpose of this oversight?

seed_items.Topic: E.071 change management control direct production change
seed_items.Stem: A developer at Northpoint Solutions made a direct change to a production database to correct a customer billing error. No change request was submitted, and the modification was not tested or reviewed by anyone else. Which IT general control is most clearly missing?

seed_items.Topic: E.072 fraud risk purchasing conflict of interest
seed_items.Stem: At Elmwood Manufacturing, the purchasing manager is authorized to add new vendors to the approved vendor master file and also selects the winning bidder for contract awards. Which control would best address the conflict-of-interest risk in this arrangement?

seed_items.Topic: E.073 monitoring exception reports not reviewed
seed_items.Stem: Sterling Company generates daily exception reports for purchasing transactions that exceed approved limits. The reports are produced automatically but no employee is assigned to review them, and exceptions accumulate without follow-up. What monitoring weakness does this reveal?

seed_items.Topic: E.074 reconciliation incompatible duties EFT and bank rec
seed_items.Stem: At Valley Associates, the same employee who initiates electronic fund transfers also performs the monthly bank reconciliation. What is the primary control weakness created by this arrangement?
seed_items.Subtopic: SoD EFT initiation vs. bank reconciliation

seed_items.Stem: Alderway ensures that the employee who approves a vendor invoice for payment is different from the employee who reconciles the accounts payable subledger to the general ledger. What does this separation help prevent?

gaps_identified.description: Zero seeds across 38 items. Internal audit function, reporting relationships, audit planning, and follow-up are completely unrepresented.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 3-4 seeds covering internal audit charter, reporting independence, audit plan development, and follow-up on audit findings.

gaps_identified.description: Zero seeds testing board independence or oversight responsibility. ED-066 tests audit committee role but not from P2 perspective.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 1-2 seeds specifically on board composition, independence requirements, and oversight duties.

gaps_identified.description: Zero seeds on organizational structure, reporting lines, or delegation of authority.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 1 seed on reporting structure and authority assignment.

gaps_identified.description: Zero seeds on commitment to competence, training, or skill assessment.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 1 seed on competence assessment or professional development requirements.

gaps_identified.description: Only 1 seed (EC-049 whistleblower) among 38. Principles 13 (relevant info), 14 (internal communication), and 15 (external communication) have near-zero coverage.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 3-4 seeds covering information quality, internal reporting flows, and external stakeholder communication.

gaps_identified.description: Only input controls covered (EC-024). Processing controls and output controls have zero coverage.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 1-2 seeds on processing controls (e.g., run-to-run totals) and output controls (e.g., report distribution).

gaps_identified.description: Only risk appetite (EC-031) and risk response (ED-016) covered. Other ERM components (objective setting, event identification, risk assessment within ERM, risk culture) are absent.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 2-3 seeds covering ERM objective setting, event identification, and risk culture.

gaps_identified.description: Only fraud triangle theory (EC-014) and whistleblower (EC-049). Proactive fraud detection techniques (data analytics, anomaly detection, surprise audits) are absent.
gaps_identified.recommendation: Add 1-2 seeds on data-analytics-based fraud detection or management review procedures.

redundancy_findings.risk: HIGH — 8 of 38 seeds (21%) test SoD in slightly different contexts. This is the dominant micro-topic. While SoD is a Core E concept, the concentration leaves other areas thin.
MODERATE — 5 seeds on IT access/change controls. EC-040 and ED-010 both test least privilege. ED-036 and ED-071 both test change management.
MODERATE — 4 seeds on monitoring/evaluation. EC-072 and ED-073 overlap (remediation vs. unreviewed reports).

coverage_balance_score.note: Coverage looks good at the LOS-area level, but drill-down reveals significant thinness within areas

veredict: Domain E has broad topic coverage across the 38 seeds but suffers from (1) SoD over-concentration (21% of seeds), (2) COSO Control Environment thinness (only P1 covered, P2-P5 absent), (3) Information & Communication near-absence (1 seed), (4) complete Internal Auditing gap, (5) ERM only partially covered. The 5-item rotation group artifact is visible in IT General Controls where Pack C and Pack D seeds mirror the same micro-topics. Recommended action: supplement with 10-15 additional seeds targeting gaps before certification.
